What It Is

A cross-check trainer that lives in your backpack.

ChairFly is an iPad app built for pilots who believe training doesn't stop at the checkride — student, private, instrument, commercial, CFI, or CFII. Instead of waiting for the next sim block, you tilt the iPad itself to fly attitude and heading, work a physical-style throttle lever, and run the same instrument scan you'd fly on an actual approach — at the kitchen table, in the FBO lounge, between flights.

It ships in two tiers, so you can start free and upgrade only when you're ready for the glass panel most training aircraft are actually moving toward.

How It Works

Four steps to a sharper scan.

No setup, no sim reservation — just the panel and a scenario.

01

Pick your panel

Start on the free 6-Pack, or unlock the Glass Cockpit for a full electronic glass panel.

02

Fly by feel

Tilt the iPad to control attitude and heading, and run the throttle lever like the real thing.

03

Run the approach

Work VOR holds and ILS approaches while scripted ATC calls vector you, just like a real clearance.

04

Check your work

Stabilize it down to minimums and you'll know — land it clean, or go around and try again.

Who It's For

Built for pilots who believe in learning.

Student, private, instrument, commercial, CFI, or CFII — the panel's worth flying at every stage. The VOR holds and ILS approaches just happen to hit hardest for instrument pilots.

Student Pilots

Start the scan early

Build cross-check habits from day one, long before instrument work is on the syllabus.

Private Pilots

Stay ready for IMC

Keep the instrument scan sharp for currency, clouds you didn't plan on, and honest decision-making.

Instrument Pilots

Where it hits hardest

Drill full VOR holds and ILS approaches until the scan is automatic — the exact reps that are hardest to get enough of before the checkride.

Commercial Pilots

Proficiency, on demand

Stay sharp between jobs and type ratings without booking sim time you don't have room for in the schedule.

CFIs

Ground school, on a screen

Pull up a scenario and walk a student through a hold or an approach before anyone straps in.

CFIIs

Teach the approach twice

Demonstrate holds, intercepts, and full approaches as many times as a student needs, without burning airplane time.

Our Goal

We want ChairFly to be the self-taught way pilots stay sharp — cheap, accessible, and small enough to fit in a backpack.

A full sim setup is expensive and tied to one location. ChairFly isn't trying to replace your CFI or your airplane — it's trying to replace the dead time in between, so every real lesson starts a little further ahead than the last one.
